subject: Hospitality
title: GOPPAR: Profit Per Room
description: A quick win: understand GOPPAR: Profit Per Room.

hook.text: Revenue is vanity, profit is sanity. GOPPAR—Gross Operating Profit Per Available Room—measures what actually stays in the bank.

buildup.text: GOPPAR subtracts operating costs from total revenue before dividing by available rooms. It shows real profitability.

discovery.text: A hotel with high RevPAR but bloated staff and energy costs might have terrible GOPPAR. Revenue alone lies about health.

twist.text: During the pandemic, hotels cut costs drastically. Some emerged with lower revenue but higher GOPPAR—leaner and more profitable.

climax.text: Investors increasingly demand GOPPAR alongside RevPAR. They want to see profit per room, not just revenue per room.

punchline.text: Revenue per room vs. profit per room. GOPPAR is the honest metric.

quiz.question: Why is GOPPAR more telling than RevPAR?
options: It measures profit per room, not just revenue—revealing true financial health
